population.definition: Conakry administrative region (entirely urban, about 450 km2, six communes), RGPH-4 2025 preliminary results with counts adjusted by the post-enumeration survey

source.title: Résultats préliminaires du RGPH-4 de la Guinée
source.quote: avec respectivement 3 407 327 habitants (19,4 %)

facts.claim: Conakry was founded from nothing in colonial times; the French settled there in 1885, when the Peninsula of Tumbo held two sparsely populated villages, Conakry and Boulbinet.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: When the French settled there in 1885, the Peninsula of Tumbo consisted of two sparsely populated villages, Conakry and Boulbinet

facts.claim: The initial site of the city was the Tumbo Peninsula, about 5 by 3 km.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: The initial site was the Tumbo Peninsula (about 5 by 3 km)

facts.claim: The Baga and the Susu, allied peoples, made up the city's initial population.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: The Baga, considered to constitute the demographic foundation of the city, and the Susu were allied peoples that made up the city’s initial population

facts.claim: Between the two World Wars the city's expansion was restricted to the peninsula, a municipal area of about 3 km2.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: it formed a municipal area of about 3 km2

facts.claim: The colonial city was built on a grid of 14 avenues numbered from the western end of the peninsula and 12 boulevards.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: The city was constructed on a grid of 14 avenues that were numbered starting from the western end of the peninsula, and 12 boulevards

facts.claim: At independence the city and its suburbs had about 70,000 inhabitants.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: At independence, the city and its suburbs had about 70 000 inhabitants

facts.claim: Conakry is the country's capital and only sizeable international harbour, an outlet for bauxite exports.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: As the country’s capital and only sizeable international harbour (an outlet for bauxite exports)

facts.claim: Kaloum is the current name of the former city centre, previously called Tumbo.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: Kaloum (the current name of the former city centre, previously called Tumbo)

facts.claim: The Conakry region covers 450 km2 and is organised into 6 urban communes and 130 quartiers (2022).

source.title: La région de Conakry en chiffres 2022
source.quote: Superficie = 450 km2

facts.claim: Conakry is 100% urban and holds a little over half (50.3%) of Guinea's urban population (RGPH-4, 2025).

source.title: Résultats préliminaires du RGPH-4 de la Guinée
source.quote: Conakry concentre un peu plus de la moitié (50,3 %) de la population urbaine du pays

facts.claim: Because the entrance to Kaloum can easily be blockaded, demonstrations are left mainly to the main roads leading from the suburbs towards the old centre.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: Since the entrance to Kaloum can be easily blockaded, the main places left for demonstrations are the main roads

timeline.claim: The French colonial establishment at Conakry dates from 1885.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: since its colonial establishment in 1885

timeline.claim: A municipality was introduced in 1904 and controlled by the colonial administration until 1956.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: Conakry had a municipality, which was introduced in 1904 and controlled by the administration until 1956

timeline.claim: A railway linked Conakry to Mamou in 1908, reached Kouroussa in 1910 and Kankan in 1914.

source.title: Guinea: colonial period
source.publisher: Encyclopedia of African History (K. Shillington, ed.), web copy
source.quote: it linked Conakry to Mamou (about 186 miles from the capital) in 1908 and reached Kouroussa in 1910 and Kankan in 1914

timeline.claim: Iron ore was extracted near Conakry from 1953 by the Compagnie Minière de la Guinée française.

source.title: Guinea: colonial period
source.publisher: Encyclopedia of African History (K. Shillington, ed.), web copy
source.quote: Iron ore was extracted near Conakry beginning in 1953

timeline.claim: Guinea voted 'no' in the September 1958 referendum on its membership of the French Community.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: the September 1958 referendum on its membership of the French Community

timeline.claim: In 1977 women organised a protest demonstration over the food crisis, breaking the pattern of the period.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: The pattern was broken in 1977 when women organised a protest demonstration over the food crisis

timeline.claim: The first stone of the Fayçal Mosque in Donka was laid in 1983.

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: although the first stone was laid only in 1983

timeline.claim: A fire in the night of 17-18 March 2018 destroyed at least 300 shops, stalls and kiosks in Madina market.

source.title: Guinée: le plus grand marché de Conakry ravagé par un incendie
source.quote: Une partie du marché de Madina, le plus grand de Conakry en Guinée, a été ravagée par un grand incendie qui s’est déclaré dans la nuit du samedi 17 au dimanche 18 mars 2018

timeline.claim: On 22 March 2023 the Prime Minister reopened the Grande Mosquée Fayçal after several years of renovation.

source.title: Culte : le Premier ministre procède à la réouverture de la grande mosquée Fayçal
source.quote: a procédé ce mercredi 22 mars à la réouverture de la grande mosquée Fayçal de Conakry

timeline.claim: The 2025 census (RGPH-4, preliminary) counted 3,407,327 people in the Conakry region.

source.title: Résultats préliminaires du RGPH-4 de la Guinée
source.quote: avec respectivement 3 407 327 habitants (19,4 %)

places.name: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve
places.what: The Nimba range is a 40 km ridge on the borders of Guinea, Liberia and Côte d'Ivoire. It is a transboundary World Heritage site listed as in danger, and home to the Nimba toad.

facts.label: World Heritage
facts.value: Inscribed 1981 (Guinea) and 1982 (Côte d'Ivoire) under natural criteria ix and x; transboundary site in danger

source.title: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve – World Heritage Datasheet
source.quote: NATURAL WORLD HERITAGE TRANSBOUNDARY SITE IN DANGER 1981 &1982: Inscribed on the World Heritage List under Natural Criteria ix and x

facts.label: Range
facts.value: A 40 km-long narrow ridge running southwest to northeast

source.title: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve – World Heritage Datasheet
source.quote: The Mount Nimba range is a 40 km-long narrow ridge running southwest to northeast

facts.label: Fauna
facts.value: More than 500 new species of fauna described in the Guineo-Ivorian reserve

source.title: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve – World Heritage Datasheet
source.quote: More than 500 new species of fauna were described in the Guineo-Ivorian Mount Nimba Reserve

facts.label: Nimba toad
facts.value: Viviparous, among the world's few tailless amphibians that give live birth

source.title: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve – World Heritage Datasheet
source.quote: one of the world’s few tailless amphibians that is totally viviparous

facts.label: Mining threat
facts.value: Kon Kweni iron-ore project planned to be carved out of the reserve (2026 report)

source.title: Leaked study warns of irreversible damage from iron ore mine in Guinea UNESCO site
source.quote: The project, named Kon Kweni, is to be carved out of Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve

places.name: Grande Mosquée de Conakry
places.what: The Fayçal Mosque in the suburb of Donka was funded and designed by Saudi Arabia and Morocco. It fell into disrepair and was reopened after renovation in March 2023.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Funded and designed by Saudi Arabia and Morocco; a building of the First Republic

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: Funded and designed by Saudi Arabia and Morocco, the large Fayçal Mosque in the suburb of Donka

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: although the first stone was laid only in 1983

facts.label: Disrepair
facts.value: In 2017: cracked walls, pierced roof, carpets removed

source.title: Guinée: polémique autour de la grande mosquée Fayçal qui tombe en ruine
source.quote: Murs fissurés, toit percé, tapis retirés

facts.label: Reopening
facts.value: Reopened on 22 March 2023 after several years of renovation

source.title: Culte : le Premier ministre procède à la réouverture de la grande mosquée Fayçal
source.quote: après plusieurs années de rénovation

places.name: Musée National de Sandervalia
places.what: Guinea's national museum stands in Sandervalia, in Kaloum, on a site named after the explorer Aimé Olivier de Sanderval. Its oldest monument is his hut, built around 1897.

facts.label: Oldest monument
facts.value: The hut (case) of Aimé Olivier de Sanderval

source.title: Arts et culture : à la découverte du Musée national de Guinée
source.quote: La case d’Aimé Olivier de Sanderval est le plus ancien monument

facts.label: Built
facts.value: Around 1897 by the French explorer Olivier de Sanderval

source.title: Arts et culture : à la découverte du Musée national de Guinée
source.quote: Elle fut construite vers 1897 par l’explorateur français Olivier de Sanderval

facts.label: Origin of the museum
facts.value: Site retained as the National Museum during a sanitation campaign under Ahmed Sékou Touré

source.title: Arts et culture : à la découverte du Musée national de Guinée
source.quote: à la faveur d’une campagne d’assainissement initiée par feu le président Ahmed Sékou Touré, le site a été retenu comme Musée national

facts.label: Courtyard
facts.value: Holds historic monuments to men and women who marked the country's history

source.title: Arts et culture : à la découverte du Musée national de Guinée
source.quote: La vaste cour du Musée national de Guinée renferme des monuments historiques des hommes et des femmes qui ont marqué l’histoire du pays

facts.label: Neighbourhood
facts.value: Sandervalia is one of the neighbourhoods whose place names inform the city's history

source.title: Conakry (chapter in Capital Cities in Africa: Power and Powerlessness)
source.author: Odile Goerg
source.quote: They included the Manquepas, Sandervalia and Coronthie neighbourhoods, whose place names provide information about the city’s history

places.name: Marché Madina
places.what: Madina is described as the largest market in Conakry and the country's largest commercial centre. It has suffered several fires, including in 2018 and 2025.

source.quote: Une partie du marché de Madina, le plus grand de Conakry en Guinée
